design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of rate_lock_extensions_and_disputes (Larkspur Home Lending, Rate Lock Commitment). Round 3.

[Step 0 — draw and scope]
draw_counts.py --task 1 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 4]}. Assignment: float-down fee (root, the borrower's own write) 6 factors; appraisal-delay waiver, relock price and relock fee 4 each.
Occupied by task 0: lock_ext_extension_request_length, lock_ext_extension_dispute_relief, lock_ext_extension_charge and their three tools. Claimed here, disjoint: lock_ext_appraisal_delay_waiver (lock_cost_waived with no dispute on file; waive_extension_charge_02e9996e), lock_ext_relock_price (lock_relocked; relock_expired_rate_20a82baa), lock_ext_relock_fee (lock_relock_fee_booked; book_relock_fee_339fcee1), lock_ext_float_down_fee (lock_float_down_fee_booked + lock_repriced; user tool exercise_float_down_fc7d974d). Every extended policy of the difficulty is claimed exactly once.
Design thesis: surface goal "use my float-down to get today's lower rate" -> hidden facts: the lock expired on 2026-10-14 (a float-down needs a locked lock -> relock first), the relock owes its fee entry before the float-down fee is worked out, and the relock fee waits on Larkspur waiving the appraisal-covered part of extension 1.

[Why it is a good test]
An agent who books the float-down straight away writes it on an expired lock with the wrong fee. To land gold it must relock at the right price (better-of for a prompt first relock, staleness, fallout and deposit adjustments), book the relock fee (back-dated extension pricing, extension step, borrower's share after the waiver, builder-partner discount) and, before that, discover that extension 1 should have been relieved for the late appraisal and value that waiver (late-correction goodwill, homebuyer-education goodwill, builder-completion offset, booked-dollar valuation because the loan amount rose). Then it hands the float-down to the borrower with the fee (improvement pricing, relocked surcharge, stage, program, loyalty and Hometown Heroes adjustments).

[Problem-tree card]
Root lock_ext_float_down_fee (on_request, owner=user). Edges:
 - root -> lock_ext_relock_price: state_gate, gate lock_float_down.float_lock_active, state form, affirmative: "A float-down is exercised, and its fee fixed, only once the lock's status reads locked." Only the relock sets an expired lock back to locked. Falsity: status expired.
 - root -> lock_ext_relock_fee: value_input, gate relocked_surcharge, state form, negated: "The float-down fee is not worked out until every relock requested on the lock's request log carries its relock fee entry." Only the relock-fee write books relock fee entries. Falsity: the 2026-10-19 relock request has no fee entry. Skip run: 2,004.18 instead of 2,560.90.
 - relock fee -> relock price: state_gate, gate rate_locks.status (a field gate, allowed for state gates), affirmative: "A relock fee is booked only after the lock's record shows the relock, the lock back in locked status with a new expiration date."
 - relock fee -> appraisal-delay waiver: value_input, gate borrower_share, negated: "The relock fee is not fixed until every borrower-borne extension charge on the lock that the appraisal-delay case covers carries its waiver entry." Larkspur's own waiver is the only write that books a waiver for the appraisal-delay case (the dispute decision relieves ordering and goodwill days only, and only for a filed dispute; none is filed here). Skip run: 445.37 instead of 222.69.
 value_input edges 2 (>= max(3-1,1)). Order: waiver and relock (commute: swapped replay gives the same terminal hash), then relock fee, then float-down.

[Base-invariant card]
Relock: relock_within_window (time; anchor rate_locks.lock_expiration_date 2026-10-14, 30 calendar days, inclusive; the 2026-10-19 request is day 5); max relocks 2 (first). Float-down: float_lock_active (true only after the relock), float_before_cd (Loan Estimate, intent to proceed and a revised Loan Estimate only); float-down unused; improvement 0.375 >= 0.25.

[Business-object card]
Lock (180-Day New Construction, expired) on the VA new-construction file. Waiver object: extension 1, the only borrower-borne extension, no dispute. Relock object: the 2026-10-19 relock request (6.750, sheet -0.875). Float-down object: the 2026-10-19 float-down request (6.375, sheet -0.625 = relocked price 0.875 less the 1.5 term adjustment). The 2019 consummated file only feeds the loyalty discount. The 2026-10-02 program-change quote explains the loan amount change (431,583.75 -> 445,374.00) behind the waiver valuation and the deposit shortfall.

[Seed timeline, checked against each owning charter]
Loan: application 2026-03-09 with its credit report fee 92.40 (a new pull: the 2019 report is long outside its validity window; VA has no application fee, so none is booked), Loan Estimate 2026-03-10, intent to proceed 2026-03-12; amount change and revised Loan Estimate 2026-10-02/2026-10-05; file conditionally approved; homebuyer education certificate on file; qualifying income 96% of area median; not a first-time homebuyer (the borrower held a home financed by Larkspur in 2019). Appraisal: standard Form 1004 order placed and opened 2026-08-24 with its 650.00 base fee charged that day, due 2026-09-02, completed 2026-09-14 (12 days late), copy delivered 2026-09-16, made subject to completion; no Form 1004D completion inspection charged yet (the home is unfinished). Credits: Builder Partner Credit reserved 2026-08-10, verified 2026-10-05 (award 1% of 436,000.00 = 4,360.00, booked); Hometown Heroes Credit reserved 2026-09-01, verified 2026-09-10 (1,000.00, booked); the two programs list each other as stackable. Lock: 180-Day lock 2026-03-16, deposit 4,315.84 received 2026-03-18, extension 1 booked 2026-09-08 under the extension-charge policy, expired 2026-10-14.

[Factor cards]
Waiver (result 1,736.96; all-baseline 1,536.54): correction_goodwill 2 (35 days after completion; -> 1,487.55), education_goodwill 2 (certificate and income <= 100% of area median; multi-source; -> 1,487.55), completion_offset -2 (subject to completion, file not clear to close; multi-source; -> 1,986.37), waiver_valuation method (loan amount rose -> booked dollars pro rata expressed in points of the current loan amount: 0.390 points; baseline per-day points 0.402 -> 1,790.40). Near-miss: the 10 Larkspur-borne days on extension 1 are its complimentary days, not appraisal relief.
Relock price (result 0.875; all-baseline 1.875): pricing_basis (method, multi-source; -> 2.125), staleness_adder 0.125 (-> 0.750), fallout_adder 0.25 (cross loan; -> 0.625), deposit_relief 0.125 (deposit short of 1% of the current amount; -> 1.000).
Relock fee (result 222.69; all-baseline 1,113.43): fee_basis method (back-dated 5 days x 3.0 bps; -> 334.03), extension_step 0.1 (-> 111.34), borrower_share 0.25 (multi-source, cross appraisal; -> 890.75), partner_discount 0.05 (cross credit; -> 276.13). Near-miss: the original 2026-09-14 expiration vs the extended 2026-10-14.
Float-down fee (result 2,560.90; all-baseline 2,226.87): improvement_pricing (method; -> 2,004.18), relocked_surcharge (-> 2,004.18), stage_surcharge (-> 2,115.53), program_adjustment (VA; -> 3,117.62), loyalty_discount (2019 file outside the 60-month window; -> 2,783.59), heroes_discount (-> 3,006.27).

[Persona]
Marisol Dunbar volunteers the float-down goal, 6.75% locked in March, 6.375% quoted this morning, the builder and a mid-November closing with no date set — all in the records. Identity: phone 6145551873 + SSN last four 2219. Passive branches only; she ends when told the lock carries the lower rate.

[Standard solution]
Locate, verify; read lock, loan files, request log, pricing ledger, deposits, disputes, appraisal order and its fees, closings, credits and credit ledger, disclosures and the file's fee ledger; waive 0.390 / 1,736.96 on extension 1; relock at 6.750 / 0.875 to 2026-11-18; book the relock fee 0.050 / 222.69; hand the float-down: 6.375, 0.575 points, 2,560.90.

[Verification]
Authoring code (scratch, removed after authoring) replayed the gold writes with the real tools, evaluated each compute on the world before its own write, substituted each factor's baseline, skipped each prerequisite and swapped the waiver and the relock. Runnable entry point: .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/env_0059_residential_mortgage_lender/tasks/rate_lock_extensions_and_disputes --task 1.

[Revision log]
Round 1: completion offset moved off a reinspection count over unseeded rows; waiver entry chosen by highest extension number (MAX); fallout adder on positive status evidence; float-down parameters re-set so the baseline differs from gold; the float-down -> relock-fee sentence made false at the opening; relock price trigger state_due.
Round 2 (policy audit):
 - T1-1 / CG-4: the waiver's valuation now fixes the waived points first and derives the dollars as points x loan amount at lock / 100, so the waiver entry keeps the base field meaning. Waived points 0.390 (unchanged), waived amount 1,737.13 -> 1,736.96; lock cost balance after the waiver 744.65; all proof text re-propagated.
 - T1-2: the homebuyer goodwill no longer rests on a first-time-homebuyer flag that conflicts with the 2019 consummated purchase; the factor is now the homebuyer-education goodwill (certificate on file and qualifying income at or below 100% of area median), and the file is seeded not first-time (first_time_homebuyer false), income 96%.
 - T1-3: the appraisal order now carries its 650.00 base fee charged on the order date (fee_balance 650.00), and the order's fee ledger is read (no completion inspection charged: the home is unfinished). Class sweep: the file's credit report fee is seeded as the loan charter books a new pull (prepaid_fee_balance 92.40) and read.
 - T1-4: the persona's passive line now reads "something has to be done on Larkspur's side", echoing no prerequisite.
 - T1-5: the fallout tier_taken text now quotes the ladder tier verbatim.
 - CG-3: the waiver policy's overwrite now names base "Second, when the loan's appraisal order was completed after its due_date, Larkspur bears as many extension days as the appraisal was late ...", replaced by its covered-days sentence; it counts the same lender-delay days already relieved (borne days beyond the complimentary days plus waiver dollars) as the extension-charge policy.
 - CG-6: the relock price's replacement sentence is now the rule's own sentence applying to every relock ("The relocked price is the pricing basis plus the staleness and fallout adders less the deposit relief, rounded to three decimal places."); the scoped sentence was removed.
 - CG-7: the relock-fee rule no longer carries a second wording of its wait ("owed as soon as the relock is recorded" removed).
 - CG-10 / CG-12: the edge effect texts are general; the borrower's share and repeat-step rules state the counts they compute.

[Difficulty-level closing — round-2 item list]
 - CG-1 / T0-1 (RED): closed — ordering clock rebuilt on charter-consistent records (weekend intent tier); task 0's appraisal order and fees dated the order date; task 0 re-laid and recomputed (dispute relief 0.160 / 1,459.84).
 - CG-2: "Larkspur bears extension days in two cases only." is superseded by three policies, each with a replacement sentence that names its own situation (a decided dispute; a clear-to-close file's booking; Larkspur's own waiver); additive, no conflict.
 - CG-3, CG-4, CG-6, CG-7, T1-1..T1-5: closed as above.
 - CG-5: closed — the extension-charge rule states and declares that every lender-delay day already relieved counts against the allowance (overwrite of the base "Second, when ..." sentence).
 - CG-8: kept by design; the two waiver writes are partitioned by whether a dispute is filed, stated in both rules.
 - CG-9 / T0-2: closed — the request edge's sentence names the exact state (a request dated later than the latest extension entry).
 - CG-10: rate_locks.status is a field gate, allowed for a state_gate edge; effect texts generalised.
 - CG-11: order_clock is an anchor method (transferred-in / Monday after a weekend intent / intent date); target_anchor changes the date counted to and adds the rescission lag in its second tier.
 - CG-12, CG-13, CG-14: closed (rule wording now states the counts; negative count taken as zero in prose and compute; extension-charge baseline carries the borne-days definition).
 - CG-15, T0-3: observations with no change needed (docstring ordinals and provenance; the wait goodwill counts calendar days by its own wording).
Union: task 0 {dispute relief, request length, extension charge}; task 1 {appraisal-delay waiver, relock price, relock fee, float-down fee} = all 7 policies; tools pairwise disjoint; each task calls one owner=user tool; no handoff in gold.
Gates after round 2 (difficulty-wide): see worklog.md.
[Difficulty-level closing — round-3 item list (render_source render_lock_r1)]
 - 1: lock_ext_extension_charge counts the Larkspur-borne appraisal-delay days in whole days, with any fraction from the waived-dollar conversion dropped (appraisal_borne = int(MX(0, ...))), and charged_days no longer truncates; the rule says so in its own words.
 - 2: the same rule states "never below zero" for the appraisal-delay days. Swept: lock_ext_appraisal_delay_waiver's base covered days get the same floor and whole-day count in compute and rule.
 - 3: the waiver's booked-basis test states "rounded to the cent".
 - 4: the full deposit relief requires "a deposit above zero" that is at least the deposit percentage of the loan amount at lock, rounded to the cent (ladder tier reworded to match). A 0% tier with nothing held now gets nothing in both prose and compute.
 - 5: the lock_relock replaced_by carries the rate half (rate stays the expired rate unless the latest relock request's rate is higher), scoped to relocks this policy prices; a lock past its window or its maximum relocks remains under the base rule.
 - 6: lock_dispute_resolution added to lock_ext_relock_price's refs, with an overwrite of its relock_pricing_disputed clause. A dispute on a relock priced here is upheld only when the rate or price is worse than this policy gives.
 - Minor (same-day surcharge): the rule and ladder say "on the current expiration date itself or later", matching notice_days <= 0.
 - Minor (five steps): the sentence now reads "Each step below adds to or subtracts from the per-day cost, and the adjusted per-day cost is never below zero."
 - Class sweep: (a) the three "two cases only" replacements (dispute relief, extension charge, appraisal-delay waiver) now carry the two base cases and name each sibling's case they leave out (CG-2 above is refined by this; the three remain additive); (b) the extension-charge cost replacement carries the cost-dollar clause and its roundings; (c) the extension-charge allowance replacement restates the as-many-days-as-late rule and its allowance; (d) the waiver's covered-days replacement is scoped to Larkspur's own waivers and leaves bookings under the extension-charge rules; (e) the float-down improvement and per-eighth points state their three-decimal rounding; (f) every compute_basis, replaced_by, prerequisite sentence and baseline sentence was checked verbatim against its rule; no overwrite retires nothing; docstrings are unchanged and carry no gold values.
 - Scored values: unchanged in both tasks (all appraisal-delay terms are already whole days; no gold deposit or notice falls on a changed boundary).
Gates after round 3 (difficulty-wide): see worklog.md.
user_scenario: You are Marisol Dunbar, 35, an Army veteran who works as a nurse in Westerville, Ohio, and you are buying a new-construction home, 1655 Meadow Lark Lane in Westerville, from Cedar Bluff Homes with a Larkspur VA loan. The builder has pushed completion back more than once and now expects to close in mid-November. You locked your rate at 6.75% back in March. This morning your loan officer told you rates have dropped a lot and that 6.375% is available today, and you remember being told your lock comes with a one-time float-down. So you are calling to use the float-down and get the lower rate on your loan today. You are warm but direct, a little tired of delays, and you want this done on this call. You are fine with the Larkspur representative handling whatever has to happen on Larkspur's side so it can go through, and if the float-down itself has to be confirmed by you in person, you will do it once they hand it to you and tell you exactly what to enter. When they ask who you are, you give your name, Marisol Dunbar, and your phone number, 6145551873; if they want a second item you give the last four digits of your Social Security number, 2219, and only if they ask for more do you give your date of birth, February 11, 1991, or your email, marisol.dunbar@outlook.com. If they ask about the house or the closing, you say the builder is Cedar Bluff Homes and that no closing date has been set yet; you do not remember the exact date your lock was last extended to. If the representative explains that something has to be done on Larkspur's side before the float-down can happen, you are surprised but you tell them to go ahead with whatever is needed. If they tell you about any charge that comes with it, you take note and tell them to go ahead. When they hand you the float-down, you enter it yourself with exactly the reference numbers, rate and fee they give you, and read back what the confirmation says. Once they confirm that your lock now carries the lower rate, you thank them and end the call. You do not know Larkspur's internal rules, you never suggest steps yourself, and you do not ask for anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.waived_points: 0.390. Valuation: the booked basis 2,481.61 / 0.575 x 100 = 431,584.35 is below the current loan amount at lock 445,374.00 (the loan amount rose), so the waived points are 2,481.61 x 14 / 20 / 445,374.00 x 100 = 0.39004, rounded to 0.390. Covered days 14 = appraisal-delay 12 (completed 2026-09-14, due 2026-09-02; allowance 30; nothing relieved before: the 10 borne days on extension 1 are its complimentary days and there is no waiver entry) + late-correction goodwill 2 (35 days after completion, > 21) + homebuyer-education goodwill 2 (certificate on file, qualifying income 96% <= 100% of area median) - builder-completion offset 2 (report subject to completion, file not yet clear to close), below the 20 charged days.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.waived_amount: 1736.96 = 0.390 x 445,374.00 / 100 = 1,736.9586, rounded to the cent. Standard method alone: 12 days x 0.02875 points = 0.345 points -> 1,536.54.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The waiver and the relock are the two prerequisites of the relock fee and do not depend on each other: the waiver writes a lock_cost_waived entry and lock_cost_balance; the relock writes status, rate, price and expiration. Replaying the relock (steps 17-18) before the waiver (steps 15-16) gives an identical terminal DB hash (True). The relock fee must follow both and the float-down must follow the relock and the relock fee (their prerequisite sentences), so the only freedom is the order of the waiver and the relock, which commute.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the relock the lock stays 'expired', so the float-down's locked-status gate fails; the terminal state lacks the relocked rate, price and 2026-11-18 expiration.
Skipping the relock fee leaves no relock fee entry: the relocked-lock surcharge falls to 0 and the float-down fee is 2004.18 instead of 2,560.90; the terminal state also lacks the 222.69 fee entry.
Without the relock the fee would be booked on an expired lock with no relock on its record; the terminal state lacks the relock and the fee entry carries the expired date and rate.
Skipping the waiver leaves no waiver entry against the borrower-borne extension: the borrower's share is 0.5 and the relock fee 445.37 instead of 222.69; the terminal state lacks the 1,736.96 waiver.
